sections.value:
# PR 237 correctness review

Head: `81f4a89974383caf7dd5bf727f3f468c0d389ed2`
Request: `01a1ec54-4541-75a2-b9c8-eac26f805be1`
Reviewer: `pij-applicable-wildcat`
Round: 1

## Verdict: BLOCK

Two P2 findings in the scoped behavior; the inherited CI blockers are separate.

## Blocking findings

**P2 — A self-asserted prime role grants cross-pane takeover authority.**
`crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs:570-572`

The new takeover gate accepts the caller's `role == "prime"` instead of the
current prime designation. A registered unrelated seat can assert that role
for itself (`http/role.rs:180-203`) and then bypass the pane-process descent
check. The new takeover test actually authorizes the prime case with only a
role assertion (`http/identity_tests.rs:2001-2016`), not a designation. This
turns a self-assignable/display role into authority to tombstone another
pane's records, contrary to the requested gate and C24's designation-only
prime authority.

Resolve the current prime designation for this gate and add a refusal case
for a caller with an asserted prime role but no current designation.
The existing lookup in `http/output.rs:487-498` uses
`state.services.directory.store().prime()` and `PrimeState::Current`.

This affects normal prime rotation too: retiring the old designation leaves
its role/live seat intact (`store/src/governance.rs:728-758`), so the former
prime can still pass this gate after a successor is designated. It requires
no caller spoofing or per-seat credentials and is not C33 hardening. Although
the role check is copied from reclaim, reclaim refuses live processes,
failed probes and live process-less records (`http/identity.rs:528-548`);
the newly added takeover does not. This PR therefore expands destructive
authority beyond that existing route.

**P2 — Failed-probe native Copilot holders bypass the takeover refusal.**
`crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:1860-1868`

For a fresh native session on a pane recorded to a different native Copilot
session, a failed liveness probe correctly adds the incumbent to
`holders.unknown` (`registration.rs:688-691`). However, when that row has its
normal native-delivery flag, local machine, nonzero process tuple and old
session, the earlier `unknown_session` branch sets `held_owner` and continues.
It never reaches the `holders.unknown` check, so the result is
`NativeSessionHold`, not the promised `E-RS-PANE-HELD` with takeover details.
An unverifiable stale native row therefore still leaves its replacement
waiting without the explicit recovery command this PR is meant to provide.

Check unknown liveness before selecting the native session hold (or exclude
unknown holders from that branch). Extend
`native_claim_supersedes_only_a_confirmed_dead_pane_holder` with an adapter
error for a different native Copilot session and assert `PaneHeld` plus an
unchanged incumbent. Its current unknown cases only cover an OMP row with no
PID and a remote OMP row (`registration.rs:2673-2689`); neither enters the
native-holder branch.

## Correctness evidence

Automatic supersession is **policy**: only confirmed `Dead` or `Recycled`
observations populate the retirement list. Missing process identities, remote
records and probe errors do not authorize retirement. The claim's ID, named
predecessor, own process and same conversation are excluded before probing.
The locked reread compares the observed ownership tuple with
`same_native_owner` before using a death witness
(`registration.rs:646-695,846-886,1277-1340,1728-1738`).

The existing drift regression covers changed incumbent/prebind ownership;
the same-session fast-restart regression pins not probing the claim's own
conversation. Ordinary registration also reaches the shared observation and
retirement path. The finding above concerns recovery/refusal selection, not
automatic retirement of an unknown process.

## CI and proof limits

CI run `44217294613`, attempt 1, names this exact head.

- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed
  (`rust-lint`).
- `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --profile ci`: 2,438 passed,
  6 skipped (`rust-test`); doctests also passed.
- Successful Rust job `134510197257` uploaded JUnit artifact `14388744100`.
  The artifact confirms that the new native dead/recycled-holder test, ordinary
  registration test, explicit takeover test, SQLite/HTTP legacy-holder test,
  and existing ownership-drift regression each ran and passed.
- Node 22: typecheck and lint passed; `npm test` had 2,301 passed and
  6 skipped; `just copilot-native-test` had 355 passed, 0 failed.
  The only failing step was `node harness/scripts/audit-gate.mjs`, reporting
  `GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf` for picomatch. PR 236 is the separate audit-allowlist
  change; this PR does not change dependencies.
- Node 24: typecheck, lint and Vitest passed; the job was cancelled during
  `just copilot-native-test`. It is not a completed native-suite pass.
- `just pr-freeze 237`: **NOT FINAL**, because merge is BLOCKED and the
  failed/cancelled checks are not green. Exact head, main base, non-draft,
  migrations and Delivers checks agreed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.

No local Cargo build or test was run, as requested. `harness boot` reported
dependency readiness false before running TypeScript or smoke. Full
`harness checks` was not run because it would invoke the prohibited local
build/test gates. CI is Linux-only; macOS behavior cannot be called tested
by these receipts. The post-deploy F196 live reproduction is still owed.

## Resource cost

No new periodic loop, poll, timer or launch site: the added pane-filtered
registry read and holder process observations occur per registration, scaling
with other live records on the claimed pane. The existing caller-descent
launches are reused only on an explicit takeover command. No live-fleet
before/after measurement or deployment was performed by this read-only review.

## Security review and platform limits

The independent read-only security review found the prime-role laundering
above. It found no target-process signal/kill path: takeover performs guarded
record tombstones. Explicit authorized takeover has no liveness guard and
retires every other process's live row on that pane, even if its process is
alive; "live holder still refuses" describes automatic registration only.
This makes the authority check materially important. Tombstoning also drops
pending FYIs and releases number claims (`store/src/registry.rs:79-102`).

The extension validates pane/holder fields and rebuilds the suggested command,
ignoring remote command text (`.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:721-774`).
`--why <reason>` is an unquoted placeholder, not a fully copy-runnable command.
The macOS connection check was source-inspected, not executed; the own-process
test covers PID equality rather than a nontrivial descendant chain.

## Harness feedback

magicWand: add the failed-probe native-holder regression described above;
it would have caught the refusal-ordering bug despite the green suites.
The review also had to distinguish passing behavior tests from an audit-only
job failure and a cancelled matrix leg manually. Preserve those distinctions
in a future exact-head CI evidence summary.
